Australia PR Points Explained (2026 Guide + Free Calculator)

Applying for Australian skilled migration? You can quickly estimate your PR score using our free PR Points Calculator to see where you stand before diving into the details below.

This guide covers everything you need to know about how Australia PR points work, what score you might need, and where to focus your efforts.

What Are PR Points in Australia

Australia PR points are a scoring system used to rank skilled migration applicants. When you want to apply for a skilled visa — such as the 189, 190, or 491 — you need to meet certain criteria, and each criterion is worth a set number of points.

The higher your total score, the more competitive your application becomes in the government's invitation rounds. Understanding Australia PR points is essential for anyone considering skilled migration, as it helps you identify which areas to improve before submitting your application.

You can explore the different visa types that use the points system on our 189 vs 190 vs 491 visa comparison page.

How the PR Points System Works

The process works in three main steps:

Step 1: Calculate Your Points

Go through each of the 12 categories and determine how many points you qualify for. Some categories are straightforward (like age), while others may require proof (like work experience or qualifications).

Step 2: Submit Your Expression of Interest (EOI)

Once you have an idea of your score, you submit an EOI through SkillSelect — the Australian government's online system. Your EOI includes your points claim and other personal details.

Step 3: Wait for an Invitation

The government runs regular invitation rounds. They invite applicants with the highest scores first, sorted by occupation. If your score is competitive for your occupation, you may receive an invitation to apply for a visa.

Note: The PR points system Australia uses is subject to change. Always check the official Department of Home Affairs website for the most current rules.

Australia PR Points Breakdown

There are 12 categories in the points test. Here is a complete breakdown:

1. Age (Up to 30 points)

Your age at the time of invitation determines your points:

  • 18–24 years: 25 points
  • 25–32 years: 30 points (highest)
  • 33–39 years: 25 points
  • 40–44 years: 15 points
  • 45+ years: Ineligible — you cannot apply for skilled migration

2. English Language (Up to 20 points)

English proficiency is one of the most important factors:

  • Competent (e.g., IELTS 6 each band): 0 points
  • Proficient (e.g., IELTS 7 each band): 10 points
  • Superior (e.g., IELTS 8 each band): 20 points

Accepted tests include IELTS, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, and Cambridge English. Note that PTE scoring thresholds changed in August 2025 — check the current requirements before booking a test.

3. Overseas Work Experience (Up to 15 points)

Skilled employment outside Australia in your nominated occupation:

  • Less than 3 years: 0 points
  • At least 3 but less than 5 years: 5 points
  • At least 5 but less than 8 years: 10 points
  • At least 8 years: 15 points

4. Australian Work Experience (Up to 20 points)

Skilled employment in Australia in your nominated occupation:

  • Less than 1 year: 0 points
  • At least 1 but less than 3 years: 5 points
  • At least 3 but less than 5 years: 10 points
  • At least 5 but less than 8 years: 15 points
  • At least 8 years: 20 points

Important: The combined total from overseas and Australian work experience is capped at 20 points. You cannot claim the maximum for both categories.

5. Educational Qualifications (Up to 20 points)

Your highest completed qualification:

  • Doctorate (PhD): 20 points
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree: 15 points
  • Australian Diploma or Trade qualification: 10 points
  • Other recognised qualification: 10 points

6. Specialist Education Qualification (Up to 10 points)

If you hold a Masters by research or Doctorate in a STEM or ICT field from an Australian institution, with at least 2 years of study, you may be eligible for 10 additional points.

7. Australian Study Requirement (5 points)

If you have completed at least 2 academic years (92 weeks) of study in Australia, you can claim 5 points.

8. Regional Study (5 points)

If you met the Australian study requirement while living and studying in a designated regional area, you may claim an additional 5 points. Distance education does not count.

9. Professional Year (5 points)

A professional year is a structured program available for Accounting, ICT, and Engineering graduates. It must be at least 12 months and completed in Australia.

10. Community Language (5 points)

If you hold NAATI accreditation at the required level (paraprofessional or above), or a community language credential, you can claim 5 points.

11. Partner Skills (Up to 10 points)

Your partner's situation affects your score:

  • Partner has skills assessment + competent English: 10 points
  • Partner has competent English only: 5 points
  • Single or partner is Australian citizen/PR: 10 points
  • Partner does not meet any criteria: 0 points

12. State Nomination (5 or 15 points)

If you are applying for a nominated visa, you receive bonus points:

  • 190 visa (state nomination): +5 points
  • 491 visa (regional nomination or family sponsorship): +15 points

Real PR Score Scenarios

To help you understand how points add up in practice, here are three realistic scenarios based on common applicant profiles:

Scenario 1: Recent IT Graduate in Australia (75 points)

  • Age 26: 30 points
  • Proficient English: 10 points
  • Bachelor's degree: 15 points
  • 2 years Australian study: 5 points
  • Single applicant: 10 points
  • Professional Year completed: 5 points
  • Total: 75 points — Competitive for 190 state nomination, borderline for 189 depending on occupation.

Scenario 2: Experienced Accountant Overseas (85 points)

  • Age 30: 30 points
  • Superior English: 20 points
  • 6 years overseas experience: 10 points
  • Master's degree: 15 points
  • Partner with competent English: 5 points
  • State nomination (190): 5 points
  • Total: 85 points — Strong for most occupations and pathways.

Scenario 3: Registered Nurse with Australian Experience (95 points)

  • Age 28: 30 points
  • Superior English: 20 points
  • 3 years Australian nursing: 10 points
  • Bachelor's degree: 15 points
  • Australian study: 5 points
  • Single applicant: 10 points
  • Regional study: 5 points
  • Total: 95 points — Highly competitive for any pathway.

What Is a Good PR Score in Australia

The minimum score to submit an EOI is 65 points. However, meeting this minimum does not guarantee you will receive an invitation. Your PR score Australia will determine how competitive you are relative to other applicants in the same occupation.

Score Ranges

  • 65–74 points: Meets the minimum, but invitation chances vary by occupation. Low-demand occupations may invite at 65, but popular ones rarely do.
  • 75–84 points: Generally competitive for many occupations, especially with state nomination. Read our detailed breakdown of what counts as a good PR score.
  • 85–94 points: Strong score across most visa pathways and occupations.
  • 95+ points: Highly competitive for any pathway, though outcomes always depend on occupation demand in each invitation round.

Score Requirements by Visa

  • 189 (Independent): Typically requires higher scores (80-90+ for popular occupations) due to no sponsorship requirement. See full 189 requirements.
  • 190 (State Nominated): State nomination adds 5 points, making it more accessible. Learn about state nomination.
  • 491 (Regional): Regional nomination adds 15 points, often the lowest threshold. See 491 requirements.

These are general observations based on recent trends. Actual invitation scores change with each round and vary significantly by occupation. Check our invitation rounds guide for the latest data.

Minimum PR Points Requirement

To submit an EOI through SkillSelect, you need a minimum of 65 Australia PR points. This is the baseline set by the Department of Home Affairs.

However, the score required to actually receive an invitation is often higher — sometimes well above 65 for popular occupations. Each invitation round has different cut-off scores depending on demand.

The government also sets occupation ceilings, which limit how many people can be invited in each occupation per year. Some occupations fill up quickly, while others may invite applicants with lower scores.

Remember: Invitation trends change regularly. The score that was enough last year may not be enough this year. Always review the latest SkillSelect invitation rounds on the official website.

How to Increase Your PR Points

Quick Improvements

  • Improve your English score. Upgrading from Competent to Proficient adds 10 points. Going from Proficient to Superior adds another 10. This is often the fastest way to boost your PR score Australia.
  • NAATI accreditation. If you speak a community language, consider getting NAATI certified for 5 extra points.
  • Professional Year. If you work in Accounting, ICT, or Engineering, completing a Professional Year adds 5 points.

Medium-Term Improvements

  • Gain Australian work experience. Each additional year of skilled work in Australia can add up to 5 points.
  • Complete additional qualifications.Upgrading from a Diploma to a Bachelor's degree, for example, can increase your education points.

Strategic Considerations

  • State nomination. Applying for a 190 or 491 visa through state nomination gives you bonus points that may make the difference.
  • Partner skills. If your partner can obtain a skills assessment and demonstrate competent English, that is worth 10 points.

What NOT to Do

  • Do not claim points for experience or qualifications you cannot prove
  • Remember that overseas and Australian work experience are capped at a combined 20 points — claiming the maximum in both is not possible
  • Do not assume your score will be enough based on old invitation data

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the minimum PR Points requirement for Australia?
The minimum score to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) is 65 Australia PR points. However, the actual score needed to receive an invitation is often higher, depending on your occupation and the visa you are applying for.
Can I combine overseas and Australian work experience for PR Points?
Yes, but the combined total from both categories is capped at 20 points. You cannot claim the full 15 points for overseas experience and the full 20 points for Australian experience at the same time.
How long does it take to get enough PR Points?
It depends on your current situation. Improving English is often the quickest path, potentially adding 10–20 points in a few months. Gaining work experience takes longer but can be more predictable. Many applicants take 6 to 24 months to optimise their profile.
Do I need a migration agent to calculate my PR Points?
No. You can estimate your score using our free PR Points Calculator or the official Department of Home Affairs calculator. A migration agent may be helpful for complex cases or if you are unsure about your eligibility.
What happens if my PR Points claim is incorrect?
If you claim points you cannot substantiate with evidence, your application may be refused. It is important to only claim points for qualifications, experience, and other criteria that you can prove with official documentation.
Can my partner's skills help increase our PR Points?
Yes. If your partner has a positive skills assessment and at least competent English, you can claim 10 additional points. If your partner only has competent English (without a skills assessment), you can claim 5 points.
How often do the PR Points requirements change?
The Department of Home Affairs reviews migration policies regularly, and changes can happen at any time. Major changes to the points system are less common, but occupation lists and invitation trends can shift frequently.
Is 70 points enough for Australia PR?
70 points meets the minimum EOI threshold, but invitation likelihood depends on your occupation and visa type. For the 189 visa, 70 may not be competitive in many invitation rounds. Consider state nomination through a 190 or 491 visa for additional points.
What is the maximum PR points Australia?
The maximum possible PR points score in Australia is 150 points when combining all eligible categories. However, work experience points are capped at 20 across both overseas and Australian experience combined. Most applicants score between 60 and 110 points.
